subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 24-year-old man with schizophrenia is brought to follow-up by his mother. Since starting treatment he no longer hears voices or believes the FBI is watching him. However, he sits expressionless for most of the day, speaks only in short one-word answers when questioned, shows little interest in previously enjoyed activities, and has withdrawn from friends.
question: Which of the following best characterizes the symptoms that persist in this patient?

options.text: Positive symptoms such as hallucinations and delusions
Negative symptoms such as blunted affect, alogia, anhedonia, and asocial behavior
Cognitive symptoms such as impaired planning and working memory
Extrapyramidal symptoms secondary to antipsychotic treatment
Dissociative symptoms with regard to identity and memory

explanation_correct: Negative symptoms reflect diminished functioning and include blunted affect, apathy, anhedonia, alogia (reduced speech output), and asocial behavior. His flat expression, one-word answers, loss of interest, and social withdrawal fit this category. Negative symptoms often persist after treatment even when positive symptoms such as hallucinations and delusions resolve, and they are a major source of long-term disability.

explanation_incorrect.A: Positive symptoms are excessive or distorted functions — hallucinations, delusions, disorganized speech, and bizarre behavior — and these have resolved in this patient.
explanation_incorrect.C: Cognitive symptoms involve reduced ability to plan, diminished working memory, and inattention; his presentation is one of diminished emotional and social output rather than a cognitive deficit.
explanation_incorrect.D: Extrapyramidal symptoms are movement disorders such as rigidity, tremor, and akathisia caused by antipsychotics, not the flat affect and social withdrawal described.
explanation_incorrect.E: Dissociative disorders involve disruptions of identity, memory, or perception, not the negative symptom cluster of schizophrenia.

educationalObjective: Negative symptoms of schizophrenia — blunted affect, alogia, anhedonia, apathy, and asocial behavior — reflect diminished functioning and often persist after positive symptoms resolve.
source: Generated from 13. Psychiatry.pdf - Pathology: Schizophrenia spectrum disorders

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 22-year-old woman reports hearing voices that comment on her actions for the past 8 months. She also has periods of disorganized speech in which her ideas drift loosely between topics. She has become withdrawn and stopped attending classes. She has no delusions and no catatonic behavior.
question: Which of the following best states the symptom-threshold requirement for diagnosing schizophrenia in this patient?

options.text: A single positive symptom is sufficient if it has lasted longer than 1 month
At least five symptoms are required, including depressed mood
Any two symptoms are sufficient, even if neither is a delusion, hallucination, or disorganized speech
At least two active symptoms are required, including at least one of delusions, hallucinations, or disorganized speech
Symptoms must include catatonic behavior and negative symptoms to qualify

explanation_correct: Schizophrenia requires at least two of the following active symptoms: delusions, hallucinations (often auditory), disorganized speech, disorganized or catatonic behavior, and negative symptoms — with at least one drawn from the first three (delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech). This patient has auditory hallucinations and disorganized speech, satisfying the threshold, plus social withdrawal. Duration criteria of at least 6 months with at least 1 month of active symptoms must also be met.

explanation_incorrect.A: A single positive symptom is not sufficient; schizophrenia requires at least two active symptoms, one of which must be a delusion, hallucination, or disorganized speech.
explanation_incorrect.B: There is no five-symptom/depressed-mood requirement for schizophrenia; that does not describe the diagnostic threshold.
explanation_incorrect.C: Two symptoms alone are not enough if neither is a delusion, hallucination, or disorganized speech — at least one of those three must be present.
explanation_incorrect.E: Catatonic behavior and negative symptoms are among the possible criteria but are not required; the key is two symptoms with at least one from the first three.

educationalObjective: Schizophrenia requires at least two active symptoms, with at least one from delusions, hallucinations, or disorganized speech, plus the appropriate duration criteria.
source: Generated from 13. Psychiatry.pdf - Pathology: Schizophrenia spectrum disorders

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 19-year-old man began hearing voices and developing bizarre beliefs 4 months ago. He also has disorganized speech and social withdrawal. His symptoms have been continuous since onset and have not required hospitalization. He has no mood symptoms and no noteworthy stressor.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Brief psychotic disorder, because symptoms began abruptly
Schizophrenia, because symptoms have persisted for more than 1 month
Schizophreniform disorder, because symptoms have lasted more than 1 month but less than 6 months
Delusional disorder, because he holds bizarre beliefs
Schizoaffective disorder, because psychosis and mood symptoms overlap

explanation_correct: Schizophreniform disorder is diagnosed when at least two schizophrenia-spectrum symptoms last 1 to 6 months. This patient has had hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized speech for 4 months, placing him in that window. Schizophrenia requires symptom onset at least 6 months before diagnosis, including at least 1 month of active symptoms. Brief psychotic disorder lasts only 1 day to 1 month.

explanation_incorrect.A: Brief psychotic disorder lasts only 1 day to 1 month and is usually stress related; his 4-month continuous illness exceeds that duration.
explanation_incorrect.B: Schizophrenia requires at least 6 months of illness with at least 1 month of active symptoms; 4 months of symptoms is too short.
explanation_incorrect.D: Delusional disorder requires at least one delusion for more than 1 month without other psychotic symptoms and otherwise intact functioning; he also has hallucinations and disorganized speech.
explanation_incorrect.E: Schizoaffective disorder requires both a mood episode and at least 2 weeks of psychosis without mood symptoms; he has no mood symptoms.

educationalObjective: Psychotic symptoms lasting 1 to 6 months fit schizophreniform disorder; schizophrenia requires at least 6 months of illness and brief psychotic disorder lasts 1 day to 1 month.
source: Generated from 13. Psychiatry.pdf - Pathology: Schizophrenia spectrum disorders

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 35-year-old woman develops auditory hallucinations and the fixed belief that her neighbors are spying on her 2 weeks after a devastating house fire. Her speech becomes disorganized. She is treated with an antipsychotic and returns to her baseline level of functioning within 3 weeks with no residual symptoms.
question: Which of the following best characterizes this patient's condition?

options.text: Brief psychotic disorder with at least one positive symptom lasting 1 day to 1 month, usually stress related
Schizophreniform disorder lasting 1 to 6 months
Schizophrenia with a good premorbid prognosis
Delusional disorder with otherwise intact functioning
Post-traumatic stress disorder with psychotic features

explanation_correct: Brief psychotic disorder involves at least one positive symptom — a delusion, hallucination, or disorganized speech/behavior — lasting between 1 day and 1 month, and it is usually stress related. This patient's psychotic symptoms began after a major stressor and fully resolved within 3 weeks with return to baseline, fitting the diagnosis. It contrasts with schizophreniform disorder (1–6 months) and schizophrenia (at least 6 months).

explanation_incorrect.B: Schizophreniform disorder requires symptoms lasting 1 to 6 months; her symptoms resolved within 3 weeks.
explanation_incorrect.C: Schizophrenia requires at least 6 months of illness including 1 month of active symptoms, which is not present here.
explanation_incorrect.D: Delusional disorder requires a delusion lasting more than 1 month without other psychotic symptoms and otherwise preserved functioning; she has hallucinations, disorganized speech, and a clear stressor.
explanation_incorrect.E: PTSD involves re-experiencing, avoidance, and hyperarousal after trauma, not a brief stress-related psychotic episode with delusions and hallucinations.

educationalObjective: Brief psychotic disorder features at least one positive symptom for 1 day to 1 month, is usually stress related, and resolves with return to baseline functioning.
source: Generated from 13. Psychiatry.pdf - Pathology: Schizophrenia spectrum disorders

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 52-year-old man is convinced that his wife is having an affair and has hired private investigators to follow her, despite repeated contrary evidence. He has no hallucinations, disorganized speech, or mood symptoms. Outside of this belief he works, socializes, and cares for his family normally. His brother, who lives with him, has recently come to share the same conviction.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Schizophrenia, paranoid type
Schizoaffective disorder
Brief psychotic disorder
Schizotypal personality disorder
Delusional disorder with folie à deux

explanation_correct: Delusional disorder is defined by at least one delusion lasting more than 1 month without a mood disorder or other psychotic symptoms; daily functioning and socialization may be affected by the belief but are otherwise intact. When a fixed delusion is shared by individuals in a close relationship, this is folie à deux. His brother's adoption of the same belief illustrates this phenomenon.

explanation_incorrect.A: Schizophrenia requires at least two active symptoms including hallucinations or disorganized speech plus significant functional impairment; he has only an isolated delusion with otherwise intact functioning.
explanation_incorrect.B: Schizoaffective disorder requires a mood episode plus at least 2 weeks of psychosis without mood symptoms; there is no mood disturbance here.
explanation_incorrect.C: Brief psychotic disorder lasts 1 day to 1 month and is usually stress related; his belief has persisted for more than a month.
explanation_incorrect.D: Schizotypal personality disorder is a cluster A disorder on the schizophrenia spectrum that may include odd beliefs and brief, less severe psychotic-like episodes, but not a single fixed delusion of this intensity with otherwise intact functioning shared by a relative.

educationalObjective: Delusional disorder features at least one delusion lasting more than a month without other psychotic symptoms and with otherwise intact functioning; a shared delusion is folie à deux.
source: Generated from 13. Psychiatry.pdf - Pathology: Schizophrenia spectrum disorders

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 19-year-old man is diagnosed with schizophrenia after 8 months of hallucinations and disorganized behavior. His brother, age 27, was diagnosed 4 years ago. Their mother asks about the typical features of this illness.
question: Which of the following statements regarding schizophrenia is most accurate?

options.text: It is more common in women, who also tend to present at an earlier age than men
Brain imaging typically shows enlarged ventricles and increased dendritic branching
It has a lifetime prevalence of about 1.5%, with earlier onset in males and an increased suicide risk
Heavy cannabis use in adolescence has been shown to reduce the incidence of psychotic disorders
It is associated with decreased dopaminergic and decreased serotonergic activity

explanation_correct: Schizophrenia has a lifetime prevalence of about 1.5%, is more common in males than females, and presents earlier in males (late teens to early 20s) than in females (late 20s to early 30s). It is associated with increased suicide risk. It is linked to altered dopaminergic activity, increased serotonergic activity, decreased dendritic branching, and ventriculomegaly on imaging. Heavy adolescent cannabis use is associated with increased incidence and a worsened course of psychotic, mood, and anxiety disorders.

explanation_incorrect.A: Schizophrenia is more common in males, and males present earlier; females have a later onset in the late 20s to early 30s.
explanation_incorrect.B: Ventriculomegaly is seen on imaging, but dendritic branching is decreased, not increased.
explanation_incorrect.D: Heavy adolescent cannabis use is associated with increased, not decreased, incidence of psychotic disorders and a worse course.
explanation_incorrect.E: Schizophrenia involves altered dopaminergic activity and increased serotonergic activity, not decreases in both.

educationalObjective: Schizophrenia has a 1.5% lifetime prevalence, affects males more with earlier onset, raises suicide risk, and is associated with ventriculomegaly, reduced dendritic branching, and heavy adolescent cannabis use as a risk factor.
source: Generated from 13. Psychiatry.pdf - Pathology: Schizophrenia spectrum disorders

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 26-year-old woman with schizophrenia has been compliant with treatment. After 6 months her auditory hallucinations and delusions have largely resolved, but she remains socially withdrawn, emotionally flat, and unmotivated. Her psychiatrist reviews her management.
question: Which of the following statements about the treatment and expected course of her illness is most accurate?

options.text: Atypical antipsychotics are first-line treatment, and negative symptoms often persist despite resolution of positive symptoms
Typical antipsychotics are preferred first-line agents because they more effectively treat negative symptoms
Negative symptoms typically resolve fully once positive symptoms are controlled
Antipsychotic treatment is indicated only during acute psychotic episodes
Cognitive symptoms are the primary target of first-generation antipsychotic therapy

explanation_correct: Atypical antipsychotics such as risperidone are first-line agents for schizophrenia. They effectively treat positive symptoms, but negative symptoms — blunted affect, apathy, alogia, and asocial behavior — often persist after treatment despite resolution of positive symptoms. This persistence is a major determinant of long-term functional outcome, as in this patient.

explanation_incorrect.B: Atypical, not typical, antipsychotics are first line; first-generation agents are less effective for negative symptoms and carry more extrapyramidal toxicity.
explanation_incorrect.C: Negative symptoms frequently persist even after positive symptoms resolve, as in this patient.
explanation_incorrect.D: Treatment is not limited to acute episodes; maintenance antipsychotic therapy is used to reduce the risk of relapse.
explanation_incorrect.E: Cognitive symptoms are difficult to treat and are not the primary target of first-generation antipsychotics, which mainly address positive symptoms.

educationalObjective: Atypical antipsychotics are first-line for schizophrenia and control positive symptoms, but negative symptoms often persist and drive long-term functional impairment.
source: Generated from 13. Psychiatry.pdf - Pathology: Schizophrenia spectrum disorders
